title: Caja-Rural’s Jaume Guardeno in intensive care after training collision with car
content:
Caja-Rural’s Jaume Gaurdeno has been hospitalised in the intensive care unit after colliding with a car while training on Tuesday.

The 23-year-old Spaniard competed in the Volta a Catalunya last week, while he was scheduled to lead Caja-Rural at the squad’s debut in the Tour de France this summer.

He finished 14th at last year’s Vuelta a Espana in a highly promising first Grand Tour.

“Our team-mate Jaume Guardeno suffered a fall last Tuesday while he was training which saw him involved in a collision with a vehicle and resulted in him being seriously injured,” read a statement from Caja-Rural.

“As a result of the accident, the cyclist from Alicante, resident in Caldes de Montbui, was urgently taken by helicopter to the Hospital Tauli de Sabadell, where he has stayed in the intensive care unit with serious injuries which are pending progress.

“From Caja Rural-Seguros RGA, we want to express all our support and strength to Jaume and his family in these moments, wishing him a swift and complete recovery. We will provide more information as his condition evolves.”

There have been several high-profile training crashes as a result of vehicles in recent years, with professional riders becoming increasingly vocal about the risks they face.

Remco Evenepoel suffered a dislocated collarbone, nerve damage, and lung contusions after colliding with the door of a postal van in December 2024, while former Tour winner Egan Bernal was nearly killed after colliding with a bus in his native Colombia in January 2022.

His team at the time, Belgian squad Soudal Quick-Step, have since changed their jerseys as part of a campaign with Safety Jogger to include more high-visibility elements.

Another former Tour winner, Demi Vollering, was the victim of a hit-and-run in Alicante this December.

Two teenage Italian cycling prospects, Sara Piffer and Francesco Mazzoleni, have already died after being hit by drivers in 2026 alone.

Government figures revealed that cycling fatalities in Spain rose from 49 in 2011 to 90 in 2023.

“As a professional cyclist the open road is my workplace, and I live the reality of the danger of cycling in traffic almost every day,” Tadej Pogacar said in 2024 as part of an international road safety campaign.

“I am not alone, as millions of people around the world ride their bikes to work, school or just for leisure. The ability for people to ride their bikes safely is something we need to protect.”
